question: How do you screen prompts, ground model outputs, and enforce approval checks when any individual classifier can miss edge cases?
paragraphs: Follow three representative requests to the exact host checkpoint where an automated check can change the outcome. Input screening, output moderation, constrained decoding grammars, and runtime tool gates stop fundamentally different failures.

When a hot-reloaded configuration fails validation, the policy engine keeps the last verified revision active. Precision and recall measurements then dictate which high-consequence tool calls must wait for human approval while audit logs record each decision cleanly without storing raw prompt secrets.
outcomes: Place runtime checks where their signals directly alter downstream execution.
Match deterministic grammars, safety classifiers, and human approvals to distinct failure modes.
Validate and version every policy change before serving production traffic.
